info.title: Enterprise GPT API
info.summary: Every endpoint the Enterprise GPT screens call.
info.description:
The API contract between the Enterprise GPT backend (Lane R, Lane K) and the interface.
Written in phase zero and wired in phase five, per `docs/plan/delivery-plan.md`. It is
published as a schema, not a document: `egpt_retail/api/models/_generated.py` is generated
from it, and the stub server in `egpt_retail/api/stub/` serves each operation's declared
examples so a screen can be pointed at the contract before any of it is implemented.

**Derived, not invented.** The endpoint inventory maps the prototype's local-storage seam
(`frontend/src/storage/*.js`) accessor by accessor, then corrects the four places where a
literal mapping would bake a demo artifact into the API (see CHANGELOG.md, 1.0.0).

**What this contract does not re-specify.** Chat, run streaming and session history are
already served by the framework and must not be duplicated here:

| Need | Framework endpoint |
|---|---|
| Chat with an agent, streamed | `POST /agents/{agent_id}/runs` (SSE) |
| Conversation history | `GET /sessions`, `GET /sessions/{session_id}` |
| Scheduled runs (definition, pause, history) | `/schedules`, `/schedules/{schedule_id}` |
| Use case definitions as versioned components | `/components` |
| Health and configuration | `GET /health`, `GET /config` |

This document adds only what those lack: the retail resources, the delivery fields on a
schedule, and the provenance record every answer writes.

**Every list is unpaginated in 1.0.0.** Phase-zero data volumes do not need it and adding
it later is additive (a `next_cursor` field). Recorded in CHANGELOG.md as a known gap.

**Semantic layer.** The `semantic` paths are the HTTP surface of Lane K's
`SemanticRead` contract (`egpt_retail/contracts/semantic.py`, v1.0.0). The stub behind
them in phase zero is `StubSemanticRead`; K5 replaces it in phase two without changing
a caller.

servers.description: The phase-zero stub server (`api/stub/server.py`'s default port, chosen so it does not collide with R1).

viewer.description: Reads dashboards, results and the catalog.

analyst.description: Viewer, plus authors use cases and KPIs and runs the playground.

admin.description: Analyst, plus activates use cases at level three and above and manages sources.

bearerAuth.description:
A JWT issued by the identity provider (Entra ID in the target deployment; an offline
RS256 key pair against a mounted JWKS file in local verification). The `scope` claim
carries the space-separated scope strings; `x-egpt-scopes` on each operation names
what it requires.

AlertDefinition.description:
A rule over a `scalar` KPI (R12): KPI, operator, threshold, scope, severity, recipient.
Evaluated by a deterministic executor after every gold materialisation. A `rowset` KPI
cannot be alerted on and is refused with 422.

window.description: How long the condition must hold before firing. Null fires on the first breach.

recommended_actions.description: Authored with the rule, rendered on every event it fires. Not generated.

use_case_id.description: The use case a fired event links to, if any.

AlertEvent.description: One firing of a definition. What the inbox, the bell and the monitor page show. Mutating it never touches the definition.

rule.description: The definition rendered as a sentence, frozen at firing time.

run_id.description: The evaluation run that fired it.

AlertEventKpi.description: The KPI reading that fired the event, frozen at firing time.

AlertScope.description: Which rows of a non-overall KPI the rule applies to.

grain_column.description:
Which gold-view column `grain_value` is matched against, when the KPI's rows carry
more than one dimension column (e.g. both `region` and `channel`) and a bare
`grain_value` could equal more than one of them. Optional and additive (CHANGELOG
1.1.2): a legacy definition with no `grain_column` is matched only when the result
set is unambiguous on shape alone -- refused, not guessed, when it is not.

AnswerBlock.description: One renderable block of an answer -- a finding, a table, a chart, a recommendation. The playground's answer format owns the inner shape; the report only needs the id and kind to pin it.

Autonomy.description: `copilot` surfaces decision cards for a person; `autopilot` executes within guardrails.

BulkProposalDecisionRequest.description: A single source harvest produces hundreds of proposals; nobody clicks through them one gate at a time (G5).

BusinessArea.description:
One node of the business hierarchy. `id` is a term from the deployment's `business_area`
vocabulary (shipped ontology plus overlay, D9/G10). `supported` is derived from confirmed
mappings (K9), never asserted; `concept_count`, `table_count` and `reason` are the
evidence behind it, so a screen can show why as well as whether.

concept_count.description: Accepted concepts in this area that have a confirmed table mapping (K9). 0 when unsupported.

reason.description: K9's one-sentence account of why the area is or is not supported, ready to render.

BusinessAreaHierarchyWrite.description: An overlay may add areas and annotate them. It may not remove or redefine a core area (G10); a request that tries is refused with 409.

BusinessAreaId.description:
A business area identifier. In 1.0.0 this is the shipped `business_area` vocabulary
(`egpt_retail/ontology/vocabularies.json`) plus whatever a customer overlay adds, so it is
a string validated at runtime against the deployment's vocabulary, not an enum.

BusinessAreaList.description: Areas this deployment supports, derived from confirmed mappings (K9). Empty means no source has been connected, never that the ontology is empty.

ChatFilters.description: The date window every answer in the playground is scoped to. Bound as the as-of window on every read, so the intro copy and the data agree.

CloudProfile.description: Where this deployment runs. Read-mostly; under D3 it is one customer's tenancy and the value is set at deploy time.

is_personal_data.description: Set by enrichment and confirmed by a person. Drives the compliance tags a provenance record carries.

sampled_values.description: Values the harvest actually saw. Bounded; never the whole column.

Concept.description: What a concept means, and how to turn it into rows. Every field arrived through a proposal a person accepted.

sql_filter.description: The SQL boolean fragment that scopes this concept. Interpolated as a PREDICATE parameter in a KPI formula. Never built from user input.

metrics.description: KPI identifiers reachable from this concept.

Confidence.description: How strongly the evidence supports a proposal or suggestion. Not a probability; a reviewer reads it to decide what to look at first.

ContentOrigin.description: Whether a document shipped with the product or is the customer's own (G17).

DeliveryChannel.description: Results are delivered in-app with an email pointer (D13). `email` and `slack` are pointers to the in-app result, never the result itself, so provenance stays attached.

DraftStep3.description: Data scope. Every id here is a configured source, a knowledge collection or a semantic table -- validated on save, so the plan cannot reference something that does not exist.

Error.description:
The error body every non-2xx response carries. `detail` is written for the person who
sees it, never a stack trace. `code` is a stable machine token so a screen can branch on
it without parsing prose.

ExternalIntegration.description: A connector source (Lane C). Its data lands in object storage against the landing contract; this record is how the interface shows it.

ExternalIntegrationPatch.description: A partial update. Every field optional; omitted fields are unchanged. Same shape as `ExternalIntegrationWrite`.

rationale.description: One sentence a customer can act on, naming the missing tables.

FeasibilityVerdict.description: The result of a set difference, never an opinion. Mirrors `egpt_retail.contracts.kpi.FeasibilityVerdict`.

FreshnessStamp.description: The stamp every gold row carries, surfaced. Without it a stale answer is indistinguishable from a wrong one.

detail.description: What to connect or confirm to close the gap. Written for the customer.

GapCheck.description: A deterministic check of the spec against the semantic layer and the KPI registry. Set differences and join-path lookups; no model is consulted.

GapKind.description:
`missing_parameter` (1.1.0, R9): a slot the chosen autonomy shape requires (build plan, section 07)
that the draft and spec do not fill -- metrics, dimensions, comparison, schedule, recipient for
Inform; candidates, guardrails, approver, write target and more for Recommend and Act. `subject`
is the parameter name; `detail` says which builder field fills it, or that none exists yet.

`unknown_grain` (1.1.1, R9): `spec.grain` is not in this deployment's grain vocabulary.
The same ground truth `spec_extractor.validate_spec` checks at extraction time, re-checked
here so a coined value is caught deterministically whether or not that validator ran first.
`subject` is the coined value; `detail` says to add it to the customer overlay or pick a
listed one.

Grain.description: A term from the deployment's `grain` vocabulary (shipped ontology plus overlay). A string validated at runtime, not an enum -- see CHANGELOG 2.0.0 of the KPI formula shape.

GuardDecision.description: What R6's SQL guard decided. A refused statement never reached the database.

Harvest.description: One run of the deterministic metadata harvest (K4). No model is involved.

source_id.description: The configured internal source that was harvested.

snapshot_version.description: The semantic snapshot this harvest produced, once it succeeded.

proposals_created.description: How many enrichment proposals the run queued for review.

InternalSource.description: A warehouse or system-of-record connection. Under D4 connectors land raw files in storage and the warehouse is loaded from there, so most deployments have exactly one `postgres` source pointed at the warehouse.

InternalSourcePatch.description: A partial update. Every field optional; omitted fields are unchanged. Same shape as `InternalSourceWrite`.

on.description: The join predicate, exactly as it would appear after `ON`.

intermediate_tables.description: Tables traversed that are neither endpoint. A preflight check needs these.

JoinPathResponse.description:
Three outcomes, never a guess. `path` present: the tables connect. `path` null with HTTP
200: the graph holds no path, which is an answer and the one a preflight check acts on.
HTTP 503: the reader could not answer, which is not an answer. **Not 404 for "no path"**
-- every HTTP client collapses 404 into "empty", which is exactly the collapse the
contract exists to prevent.

Kpi.description:
One KPI, as the registry holds it (K11) and the discovery screen renders it. The formula
fields are the contract shape; the presentation fields are what the registry screen shows.
`feasibility` is embedded so the list renders its ready/partial/blocked badges without a
call per row -- it is still a set difference, computed on read, never stored.

identifier.description: `<concept>__<name>`, stable across edits. What provenance and gold rows reference.

sql.description: The formula with `{named}` placeholders. Returned only to callers holding `kpis:write`; a viewer sees the field absent.

KpiComputeResult.description:
The outcome of materialising one KPI for today's business date on demand -- the same
guarded pass the nightly run performs (`materialise_gold`), narrowed to one identifier.
`materialised` wrote today's row(s) and `GET /kpis/{kpi_id}/series` now has today's point;
`failed` names the formula's own error; `skipped` names why the pass would not run it.

KpiComputeStatus.description: Mirrors `gold.kpi_run.status` for the one KPI the call materialised.

KpiHealth.description: Freshness from gold (R5). Every gold row is stamped with source and computation time; this is that stamp surfaced.

as_of.description: The bound as-of date the last materialisation computed against.

KpiImportRequest.description: The CSV import panel. One row per KPI; columns match `KpiWrite` field names. Rows that fail construction are reported, not silently dropped.

KpiOrigin.description: Whether the KPI shipped with the product or the customer authored it.

KpiSeries.description:
One KPI's value over its last business dates, read from `gold.kpi_value` -- the same rows
a dashboard's `line`/`bar` tile plots, addressed by KPI rather than by tile. One point per
business date the KPI materialised for; a night with no row is absent, not `null` (`null`
means the formula returned NULL that night). Nothing is recomputed on read.

A KPI whose grain is not `overall` has one row per dimension value each night; `dimension`
names the one the points follow (the caller's choice, else the first seen) and
`dimensions` lists every value the latest night carried, so a screen can offer the others.

days.description: The window the points were read over, ending at `as_of`.

dimension.description: The grain-key values the points follow; `null` for an `overall` KPI.

dimensions.description: Every dimension the latest business date carried, in gold's row order, capped at 25.

value.description: The latest point's value; what a `number` tile of this KPI shows.

delta.description: `value` minus the previous point's value; `null` with fewer than two points.

KpiSeriesInterval.description: The spacing of `KpiSeries.points`. Gold materialises once a night (D7), so `day` is the only interval today; a coarser one would be an aggregation this contract does not define.

KpiSource.description: A user-added dataset in the KPI gallery (kpi-sources.js). More than a connection -- it carries the business context that turns rows into metrics.

source_id.description: The configured internal source it comes from, if known.

KpiSuggestion.description: A candidate KPI proposed by the K12 agent. Typed for direct rendering; every closed-set value from the deployment's vocabulary; traceable to named tables or it was invented.

rationale.description: One sentence naming the tables or concepts it derives from.

notes.description: Empty on a clean run; otherwise what was missing (the skill template's refusal shape).

KpiSuggestionRun.description:
One run of the K12 suggestion agent, started by `POST /kpis/suggestions` and polled at
`GET /kpis/suggestions/{run_id}` (#254). A run is two frontier-tier model calls and can
take minutes, so it is not served inside a request. `result` is the same
`KpiSuggestionList` the synchronous route returns, present once `status` is `succeeded`;
`error` is why there is none, present once `failed`. A run whose executor was lost
(the serving instance restarted mid-run) is reported `failed` by the read side after the
deployment's timeout plus a grace period, never `running` forever.

Two fields are for the person waiting: `phase` is the stage a `running` run is in, and
`typical_duration_seconds` is how long this deployment's recent runs took, so a screen
can set an expectation up front and show progress against it.

business_area.description: The area the run was narrowed to, or null for every area.

error.description: Written for the person polling. A timeout names the bound it hit.

phase.description:
Set while `running`, as each stage begins; null on a `queued` run and on a
`running` one that has not reached its first stage yet. Kept as it was once the run
is terminal, so a `failed` run says where it failed.

typical_duration_seconds.description:
The median wall-clock seconds of this deployment's last few successful runs, or null
before any has succeeded. An expectation, not a bound: a run may take longer, and the
deployment's timeout is the only limit.

KpiSuggestionRunPhase.description:
The stage a `running` suggestion run is in, in order: `reading` (the semantic layer the
agents are shown is being gathered), `proposing` (the model calls), `checking` (assembly
and feasibility against the snapshot). What a screen's stepper shows.

KpiSuggestionRunRequest.description: What to run. Empty means suggest across every business area.

KpiSuggestionRunStatus.description: Where a suggestion run is. The same four words as `HarvestStatus`, for the same shape.

KpiWrite.description: Authoring a KPI. The formula is validated at construction (declared parameters match placeholders, source tables cover the formula) and refused with 422 naming the defect.

ModelTier.description: Which R8 routing tier this deployment binds the model to. Two deployments, composed through the escalation provider (G6).

Operator.description: `delta_*` compares the change against the previous period at the same grain.

ParameterKind.description: `predicate` is an interpolated SQL fragment from an accepted proposal; `scalar` is a driver-bound value. Never interchangeable.

PermissionLevel.description: The database role the source is connected with. `read_only` is the floor R6's guard sits on; a `read_write` source is never exposed to a model.

Plan.description: A view over the compiled workflow, never authored separately. Steps four and five of the prototype's wizard render this.

PlanStep.description: One step of the compiled workflow. `ref` is an executor name from the registry or a skill identifier -- the same strings the stored workflow holds.

permits_or_blocks.description: True for the executors that can stop the run -- preflight, guard, feasibility. Always false for an agent step, by the alignment rules.

PreflightResult.description: Whether the use case may run now. A deterministic executor's answer; if it blocks, the reason is one a person can act on.

blocked_by.description: Names of the checks that failed.

Process.description: A named operational process within a business area. Read-only in 1.0.0 (see CHANGELOG).

Proposal.description:
One thing an agent proposed, and the record of what happened to it (K7,
`semantic.proposals.Proposal`). `target` is a plain string -- a concept name, a qualified
table, or (for `kind: kpi`) a metric identifier -- and `payload` carries whatever that
kind needs to be applied, which is why its shape is not fixed here: a `kpi` payload is a
whole KPI definition (`identifier`, `name`, `sql`, `grain`, `business_area`,
`source_tables`, plus display-only fields a reviewer wants -- `rationale`, `feasibility`,
`feasibility_reason`, `missing_tables`); a `use_case` payload is a question and the KPIs
it depends on. Nothing here reaches the graph, or the KPI registry, until `state` is
`accepted` (D10, G5) -- and even then, `applied_at` is what says whether it actually
landed, not `state` alone.

proposer.description: Which agent or person produced it. Never blank.

applied_at.description:
Set only once an accepted proposal's effect actually landed (a KPI saved to the
registry). An `accepted` proposal with `applied_at: null` is accepted-but-not-yet-
landed, or a kind with no consumer today (`use_case`) -- never assume `accepted`
alone means "done".

ProposalCounts.description: Totals by state, so the review screen can show its badge without a second call.

ProposalDecision.description: K7's `ReviewState`. One way out of `pending`, and no way back.

note.description: Optional reviewer note, kept with the decision.

ProposalKind.description:
What a proposal is about (K7's closed set, `semantic.proposals.ProposalKind`). `kpi` and
`use_case` are what `egpt-retail suggest` files; the other five are K4/K8 harvest-time
enrichment kinds this review screen also lists but does not specially render.

refused.description: Ids from the request that were not pending and so did not move. Empty on a plain list read.

ProposalRefusal.description:
One id in a decision request that did not move, and why. A bulk decision is not
atomic (K7's own `ReviewOutcome`, deliberately: eleven good decisions committing must
not be held hostage by a twelfth id a colleague decided a moment earlier) -- this is
how the caller finds out which one, and what its actual state is.

ProposalStatus.description:
Whether a row has been through review. Only `accepted` rows reach the graph (D10, G5).
A `proposed` row is returned only to a caller that passed `include_proposed=true`, and it
arrives labelled, so there is no way to receive an unreviewed synonym and mistake it for
a confirmed one.

Provenance.description:
The record every answer writes (alignment rule: "every answer writes a provenance
record"). Its shape is fixed here in phase zero so that R7 implements it rather than
designs it, and so the citation panel in the playground renders one thing. Holds what was
read, what was executed, what was sampled, how fresh each input was, what retrieval
returned, and which model tier answered.

semantic_snapshot.description: The semantic snapshot version every read in this run was answered from.

vocabulary_version.description: The shipped vocabulary version closed-set values were validated against.

ProvenanceModelTier.description: `none` when the run had no model step at all.

address.description: An email address or a Slack channel. Empty for `in_app`.

RefreshSchedule.description:
How often the dashboard's numbers are recomputed -- the declared cadence, stored for the
scheduler to honour. `nightly` (the default) follows gold: as soon as the nightly
materialisation completes (D7). `daily` is once a day at a fixed morning time (06:00),
reading what gold holds. `weekly` is Monday mornings. `hourly` is every hour, capped in
practice by how often gold materialises. `manual` is only when asked. Distinct from
delivery (who is sent what, and when), which this contract does not yet carry.

run_id.description: The run the block came from, so its provenance is one hop away.

ResultShape.description: Mirrors `egpt_retail.contracts.kpi.ResultShape`. A `rowset` cannot be alerted on or trended.

RetrievalSource.description: The four legs the unified retrieval fans out across (K10).

ScheduleDelivery.description: The delivery fields a framework `/schedules` row lacks. Everything else about a scheduled run -- cadence, pause, history -- is the framework's.

SkillRef.description: Which skill, at which version, produced something. Every prompt edit bumps the version, so a score drop is attributable (G13).

Snapshot.description: Which semantic version a read was answered from. On every response.

Spec.description:
What the author asked for, extracted by the spec-extraction agent (R9, Lane R's first
skill). Every closed-set value comes from the semantic layer and the vocabulary; an entity
the deployment does not have cannot appear here, it appears in `notes` instead.

notes.description: Empty on a clean extraction; otherwise what the question asked for that the deployment cannot express.

questions.description:
Clarifying questions for the author (1.1.0, R9). Where `notes` records what could not be
expressed, this records what the agent needs answered before the spec is complete -- a
metric it could not match to the registry, or a sentence ambiguous about whether the use
case should act. Empty on a clean extraction. A question is the refusal shape for an
unknown; the agent never coins a value to avoid asking one.

concept.description: A concept name from the semantic layer. Closed set, rendered from `GET /semantic/concepts`.

concepts.description: Ontology concepts this table is an instance of, once mapping is confirmed (K8).

TableRef.description: A table's identity without its columns. What listing returns.

TermOrigin.description: Whether the shipped ontology or the customer's overlay contributed a term (G10). Mirrors `egpt_retail.contracts.vocabulary.TermOrigin`.

grain_value.description: For a KPI at a non-overall grain, which row -- a supplier id, a location -- this tile shows. Null shows the top-N as a table.

TileData.description: One tile's values from gold, with the stamp every gold row carries so a stale number is distinguishable from a wrong one.

delta.description: Change against the previous period at the same grain.

rows.description: For a `rowset` KPI or a table chart.

TimeWindow.description: A declared lookback relative to the run's as-of date. Never written into the SQL, so yesterday's number can be recomputed.

UseCase.description:
A use case is three artifacts -- a stored workflow component, the skill prompts its agent
steps carry, and a spec record holding what the author asked for. This is the catalog view
over all three. `level` is the autonomy level the activation screen shows; activating at
three or above needs the admin role (G11).

workflow_component_id.description: The framework component (`/components`) holding the compiled workflow, once one exists.

version.description: Bumped on publish. Runs and golden sets are attributed to a version (R15).

UseCaseDraft.description:
The builder's working state, steps one to nine. Persisted as a whole because the wizard
reads and writes it as a whole. Steps four and five (`plan_items`, `tasks`) are deliberately
absent: they are derived views served by `GET /use-cases/{id}/plan` over the compiled
workflow, never authored here -- a plan authored in parallel with the workflow is the
failure the build plan names.

UseCaseExecutionHealth.description: Execution health, from persisted run history. Free -- nothing here needs an assessment pass.

silent.description: The schedule should have fired and did not.

gates_waiting.description: Approval gates waiting on a person longer than their threshold.

error.description: Set instead of a real health snapshot when this one use case's own entry was malformed (e.g. a missing workflow_id) and its processing was isolated rather than aborting every other use case's report. Absent/null for a genuinely-run or genuinely-never-run use case.

UseCaseQuality.description: Is it still right -- the assessment pass over output quality and input drift (R14), separate from whether it ran. A use case that runs green while answering worse is what this catches.

golden_pass_rate.description: Share of the golden questions (R15) that passed on this version.

drift_score.description: Input distribution drift against the version's rehearsal baseline. 0 is none.

UseCaseRun.description: One run, keyed by use case and version (G12), holding its status, output reference and provenance reference. What "why did last Tuesday's run say that" hits.

framework_run_id.description: The framework's run id, for the session and run-history endpoints.

output_ref.description: Where the delivered answer lives -- a report id, or a knowledge document id once ingested (G12).

UseCaseSource.description: Whether the entry shipped with the product as a template or the customer authored it.

UseCaseSuggestion.description: A use case proposed from the connected data and the catalog (K13). Shares inputs and output discipline with KPI suggestion.

template_id.description: When creating from a template, the template's id; the draft is prefilled from it.

row itself -- a suggestion becomes a KPI only through `POST /kpis`, so this needs

body suggests across every area.

get.description: The rows the nightly run materialised for this KPI over the last `days` business dates, one point per night that has a row -- what the discovery detail panel graphs after a KPI is adopted. A read of `gold.kpi_value`, never a recomputation, so a KPI adopted today has no point until it is computed (`POST /kpis/{kpi_id}/compute`, or tonight's run). A KPI with a grain other than `overall` follows one dimension at a time; `dimension` picks it, else the first seen.

post.summary: Accept many proposals in one decision. Not atomic -- see the response's `refused`.
post.description:
A harvest or a suggestion run produces many proposals at once; a gate per proposal is the
obvious tool and the wrong one (G5). **Deliberately not all-or-nothing**: an id that is
no longer pending (someone else decided it a moment earlier) is skipped and reported in
`refused`, and every other id in the request still commits -- eleven good decisions must
not be held hostage by a twelfth (K7's `ReviewOutcome`). Any `kind: kpi` ids that did
commit are adopted into the registry in the same call, same as the single-accept route.
Always `200`; check `refused` to see whether every id in the request actually moved.
